sources.title: How My Predictions Are Faring — Ray Kurzweil
sources.locator: The Computer Itself, prediction 14, printed p. 22

sourceCaveat: The original book edition has not been independently checked. See the listed source on Sources for attribution limits.

strict.criterion: More than half of generated text comes from continuous-speech dictation.
strict.rationale: The author’s own retrospective acknowledges that dictation had not become the majority input method in 2009. Dictation is effective and widely available, but typing and non-dictated text remain central. The majority claim is still not supported; this assessment is an inference, not a global text-volume census.

broader.criterion: Accurate everyday speech dictation is widely available and used as a meaningful secondary text-input method.
broader.rationale: Modern voice-to-text on phones and computers is accurate and widely used, so the underlying speech capability succeeded. Even charitably, however, typing remains the primary way people produce text, and rewriting 'majority of text' into 'dictation exists' discards the prediction's core claim.
changedConditions: Credits widespread practical dictation capability as partial without counting it as a majority-of-text hit
